hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker consumes notifications.outbound and processes normally for about 3 minutes after starting v1.8.8 (#1340), then crashes with a stack overflow in expandReferences on msg-364842 at offset 371126 (#1802). Every restart resumes at the same committed offset 371126 (#1834, #1911, #2053, #2293), so the worker redelivers the same message and crash-loops. Restarts continue with increasing backoff (#1804, #1853, #1938, #2076). Lag on notifications.outbound grows because the consumer never gets past this offset. The upstream timeouts are a separate issue and not the notif-worker cause.

The crash loop began about 2m50s after notif-worker v1.8.8 (build 271d647) rolled out (#1268, #1340). The new release's expandReferences code recurses without a depth limit, which is the likely code-level defect. The worker handled roughly 100 batches on v1.8.8 before hitting this message, so the release is not broadly broken; the trigger is a single input. Rollback or a hotfix would also stop the crash.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately skip or dead-letter msg-364842 at notifications.outbound offset 371126 so the consumer can advance, and inspect that payload for deeply nested or self-referencing references. In parallel, roll back notif-worker to the pre-v1.8.8 build or hotfix the unbounded recursion in expandReferences, and add a depth guard and a dead-letter path for poison messages. Separately, report-cron is failing on image report-cron:2026.10.2 with a missing pandas module (#1220), which is unrelated to this alert but needs its own fix.

Every restart resumes at the same committed offset 371126 (#1834, #1911, #2053, #2293), so the worker redelivers the same message and crash-loops. Restarts continue with increasing backoff (#1804, #1853, #1938, #2076). Lag on notifications.outbound grows because the consumer never gets past this offset. The upstream timeouts are a separate issue and not the notif-worker cause.

The crash loop began about 2m50s after notif-worker v1.8.8 (build 271d647) rolled out (#1268, #1340). The new release's expandReferences code recurses without a depth limit, which is the likely code-level defect. The worker handled roughly 100 batches on v1.8.8 before hitting this message, so the release is not broadly broken; the trigger is a single input. Rollback or a hotfix would also stop the crash.
